stories.headline: Oksana Dudar: ‘I told him it’s better to be the widow of a hero than the wife of a coward’ Her grief at the death of her husband four years ago seemed emblematic of the grief of Ukraine. Yet, like her country, she is moving forward with a sense of pur
stories.summary: Oksana Dudar's grief over her husband's death four years ago symbolized Ukraine's collective grief. Her husband's death occurred during a time of conflict, and she had reportedly told him that it's better to be the widow of a hero than the wife of a coward. Despite her loss, Oksana is moving forward with a sense of purpose, much like her country, which continues to navigate the ongoing war. Oksana is also a musician, with her music available on platforms like Apple Music, where her top songs and albums can be found. Her story serves as an example of resilience and determination in the face of adversity, reflecting the broader experiences of Ukrainians affected by the conflict. Oksana's music and story are now being shared with a wider audience through various online platforms.

stories.headline: Andes hantavirus outbreak highlights global spillover and transmission risks A Virginia Tech disease ecologist said the outbreak of Andes hantavirus aboard the international MV Hondius cruise ship underscores how little scientists still
stories.summary: An outbreak of Andes hantavirus occurred aboard the international MV Hondius cruise ship, resulting in three deaths and potentially sickening several more among the approximately 150 passengers. The ship was on a weeks-long polar cruise when the outbreak happened. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) issued a Health Alert Network advisory to inform clinicians and health departments about the new cluster of hantavirus disease cases caused by infection with Andes virus. According to Luis Escobar, a disease ecologist at Virginia Tech, the outbreak highlights the limited knowledge scientists have about viruses circulating in wild rodent populations before they spill into humans, and the failure of current public health models to predict such spillover events. The incident underscores the global risks of spillover and transmission of zoonotic diseases like hantavirus.

stories.headline: ‘It’s like we went bankrupt overnight’: poorest Somalis suffer as piles of worthless shillings mount up Banknotes are now so tattered that even buses refuse to accept them, as a dollarised economy and mobile phone payments push up the cost of essentials
stories.summary: Somalia's economy is experiencing a crisis as its banknotes become increasingly worthless and tattered. Even buses are refusing to accept them, forcing people to rely on alternative forms of payment. The country's shift towards a dollarized economy and mobile phone payments has driven up the cost of essentials, exacerbating poverty. Millions of Somalis are expected to suffer as a result, with more families being pushed into poverty. The devaluation of the Somali shilling has left many without a viable means of exchange, making everyday transactions a challenge. The situation is dire, with many Somalis struggling to access basic necessities due to the worthless currency. As the economy continues to deteriorate, the poorest Somalis are bearing the brunt of the crisis, facing increased hardship and uncertainty.

stories.headline: Peanut farmer-intellectual Jimmy Carter was just what Americans needed. They still need his ilk There is a neat symmetry to Carter’s story and to his hometown’s quietly glowing presence in the US
stories.summary: Jimmy Carter, the 39th US president, was a peanut farmer from Georgia who remained prominent on the world stage after his presidency. He died on December 29, 2025. Carter was known for his candor, stubbornness, and commitment to his principles. After leaving the White House, he wrote over 30 books, including bestsellers, to pay off a $1 million debt accumulated by his peanut business. He also worked with former presidents on the One America Appeal to help victims of natural disasters. Carter's legacy is one of leadership, empathy, and humanitarianism, demonstrated through his actions as a president, peace-builder, and global humanitarian. His passing marks the end of a century-long journey, but his legacy will live on, remembered for his quiet and steadfast dedication to others. Carter's story and hometown have a lasting presence in the US, symbolizing his enduring impact.

stories.headline: AI-Powered Automatic Tab Groups Reportedly Coming to Safari via iOS 27, macOS 27
stories.summary: Apple is reportedly introducing an AI-powered feature to Safari, allowing for automatic tab groups in iOS 27, macOS 27, and iPadOS 27. The feature, currently in internal testing, automatically organizes browser tabs into topic-based groups, eliminating the need for manual sorting. This new capability builds upon existing Tab Groups, providing a practical application of AI for everyday browsing. The feature is similar to Chrome's AI-powered tab organization tools, which sort related pages together. According to Bloomberg's Mark Gurman, Apple has started testing this feature, expected to roll out with the upcoming iOS 27, iPadOS 27, and macOS 27 updates. The AI-powered automatic tab grouping aims to help users better organize their browsing sessions, making it easier to manage multiple tabs. The feature is expected to enhance the overall browsing experience in Safari.

stories.headline: iPhone 18 Pro Max launching this year and this is how much it may cost
stories.summary: Apple's iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max are expected to launch later this year without a major price hike in the US. According to analyst Jeff Pu, the base storage variants of the Pro models will have "aggressive pricing". The iPhone 18 Pro Max may start at $1,199 in the US, maintaining last year's pricing despite rising production costs. The switch to 2-nanometer processors from TSMC could increase chip costs by $35, but Apple may absorb this cost to remain competitive. The new iPhones will be part of a larger lineup, including the iPhone Fold, which could cost upwards of $2,000, and the standard iPhone 18 and iPhone 18e, which will be introduced after the fall launch of the Pro models. The pricing strategy aims to help Apple strengthen its position against Android rivals.

stories.headline: Mind xPlay display and keyboard review using Khadas Mind and Mind 2 mini PCs
stories.summary: Khadas has released the Mind xPlay, a portable display and keyboard designed for mobile workflows. The device features a 13-inch, 1080p screen, 2MP webcam, stereo speakers, and dual microphones. It can be used as an external display for devices like the Mind and Mind 2 mini PCs, as well as laptops. The Mind xPlay has a detachable keyboard and battery, offering better portability for workflows than laptops or mini PCs. It can transform the Mind Pro into a notebook and is also compatible with other devices. Khadas has also teased a new concept device, the Mind Go, a 3-in-1 computer with a thin tablet, detachable keyboard, and docking station. The Mind xPlay aims to solve the pain point of switching workflows between fixed locations, providing a precise fit for high-performance mobile workflows.

stories.headline: The month that was April | Gavelled! A Ferrari V12 GT, a piece of Porsche history and a Richard Burns special headlined auctions in April
stories.summary: Auction houses saw notable sales in April, with a Ferrari V12 GT, a piece of Porsche history, and a Richard Burns special being top headliners. The month's auctions featured a range of desirable cars, including rare Ferraris and Porsches. A 1979 Ferrari 308 GTS from the TV show 'Magnum, P.I.' was auctioned by Barrett-Jackson. Other notable lots included a 1995 Sbarro Alcador Roadster, a 2006 Ferrari 575 Superamerica, and a 1953 Mercedes-Benz 220 Cabriolet A. A single-owner 918 Spyder, offered with its original accessories, represented an investment-grade opportunity to own a piece of Porsche's technological history. These sales followed a strong year for Bonhams|Cars, which sold landmark Ferraris, record-breaking hypercars, and other rare vehicles in 2025. The Scottsdale Auction traditionally kicks off the US collector-car scene, with Bonhams|Cars offering a balanced catalogue of classics and emerging collectibles.

stories.headline: Marcus Rashford: Man United loanee scores sublime free kick in El Clasico
stories.summary: Marcus Rashford scored a sublime free kick in El Clasico, helping FC Barcelona secure a 2-1 win over Real Madrid and seal the La Liga title. The Manchester United loanee's goal came just nine minutes into the match, increasing his season tally to 14. Rashford has been impressive for Barcelona, and his performance has led him to express his desire to stay with the club. He has urged Barcelona to make his £26m loan move permanent. Rashford's free kick was a notable highlight of the match, and his overall performance has been praised as he continues to develop as a player during his time with the Spanish club. His goal contributions have been significant, and he is reportedly keen to extend his stay with Barcelona beyond his current loan spell.

stories.headline: Wayne Rooney says VAR did 'a really good job' in making a crucial call in Arsenal's win at West Ham
stories.summary: Wayne Rooney praised the VAR system for making a crucial call in Arsenal's win at West Ham, saying it did "a really good job". The decision in question was the disallowing of a West Ham goal in injury time, which helped Arsenal go five points clear. Rooney acknowledged the correct decision was made, but also expressed concern about the advantage goalkeepers have inside their own area. Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta had a different view, stating the VAR decision "could've gone either way". The win was significant for Arsenal, increasing their lead in the standings. The VAR call was a key moment in the match, and its accuracy was applauded by Rooney, a former professional player.

stories.headline: Nicky English: Cork get expected win but in unexpected circumstances Waterford undermined by injuries but battle to the end while Offaly present further evidence of their resurgence
stories.summary: Cork secured an expected win over Waterford, but in unexpected circumstances, as Waterford battled to the end despite being undermined by injuries. Waterford lost key players Ian Kenny, Iarlaith Daly, and Stephen Bennett to injury in the first half, which further impeded their chances. Cork's Brian Hayes scored seven points, while Tim O'Mahony, Darragh Fitzgibbon, Niall O'Leary, and Mark Coleman also delivered strong performances. The result leaves Waterford on the brink of elimination before their trip to Limerick. If Clare beats Tipperary next Saturday, Waterford will be eliminated and have nothing to play for in their next match. Cork's win marks their first ever three-in-a-row of Munster round-robin wins in the same summer. The outcome highlights Waterford's ongoing struggles and Cork's continued momentum in the competition.

stories.headline: Black Stars players are highly motivated ahead of Mexico friendly - Desmond Ofei
stories.summary: Ghana's Black Stars are highly motivated ahead of their friendly match against Mexico on May 22. The game is part of their preparations for the 2026 World Cup, which will be held in North America this summer. Assistant coach Desmond Ofei stated that the team is in high spirits and fully motivated for the encounter. A 23-man squad has been assembled by the technical team, led by head coach Carlos Queiroz. The friendly match provides an opportunity for players to impress the new head coach ahead of the World Cup. The game will be played in North America, with the 2026 FIFA World Cup scheduled to take place across the United States, Canada, and Mexico later this summer. The Black Stars are using this match as a key part of their build-up to the global tournament.

stories.headline: Modi says Iran war poses severe risks to India, urges cuts in fuel use and gold purchases
stories.summary: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi has urged citizens to reduce fuel consumption, overseas travel, and gold purchases due to the economic impact of the US-Israeli war on Iran. Modi appealed to Indians to work from home, use public transport, and cut down on non-essential expenses to conserve fuel and foreign exchange. The austerity measures aim to mitigate the effects of oil shortages and price spikes, as India imports 90% of its oil. The prime minister also asked families to reduce cooking oil consumption, describing it as a healthy and patriotic move. Additionally, he advised against buying gold and non-essential overseas travel for at least a year to help save foreign exchange, amid a multi-billion dollar spike in India's crude oil bill.

stories.headline: Modi Asks Indians to Stop Buying Gold, Hitting Jewelry Stocks
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi has urged Indians to refrain from buying gold for at least a year to conserve foreign-exchange reserves. This appeal is significant in a country where gold plays a crucial role in savings, weddings, and religious festivals. Following Modi's announcement, jewelry stocks experienced a sharp decline, with some plummeting up to 12% in intraday trading. Investors reacted to concerns that demand for gold could slow, particularly during weddings and festive seasons, which are key drivers of the industry's sales cycle. The sudden sell-off in jewelry stocks reflects the market's immediate response to the prime minister's message, highlighting the potential impact on the gold industry in India. The call to avoid gold purchases aims to preserve foreign-exchange reserves, amid escalating concerns.

stories.headline: US lobbying disclosures puncture Asim Munir's India-Pakistan May ceasefire claim
stories.summary: Pakistan Chief of Defence Forces Asim Munir claimed India approached the US for a ceasefire during Operation Sindoor. However, US lobbying disclosures contradict this statement. According to FARA filings, Pakistan lobbied US lawmakers during the same period, indicating an intense diplomatic effort by Islamabad. Munir's claim surfaced nearly a year after the operation, despite him making inflammatory statements against India beforehand. The lobbying disclosures suggest Pakistan was actively engaging with US officials, contradicting Munir's assertion that India sought mediation. The discrepancy raises questions about the accuracy of Munir's statement, which was made at an event where he claimed India sought US intervention to cease hostilities. The US lobbying records provide a different narrative, highlighting Pakistan's own diplomatic efforts during the time.

stories.headline: Newly elected Tamil Nadu MLAs take oath in Assembly amid a historic session
stories.summary: Newly elected Tamil Nadu MLAs took oath in the Assembly amid a historic session. The oath-taking ceremony was initiated by Pro-tem Speaker M V Karuppaiah, who praised Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay's leadership and victory. Vijay, along with other newly elected MLAs, including those from Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK), took oath as legislators. After taking oath, the members signed in the Assembly register. The first session of the 17th Assembly convened, with the Speaker election scheduled for May 12. The MLAs were elected in the legislative assembly elections held on April 23, 2026, with results declared on May 4, 2026. The ceremony marked the beginning of the new government formation in Tamil Nadu, with Vijay at the helm as Chief Minister. The Assembly session is a significant step towards the formation of the new state government.

stories.headline: Bitcoin trades near $81K despite strong US jobs data; ETF inflows and CLARITY Act optimism support sentiment
stories.summary: Bitcoin traded near $81,000 on Monday, despite strong US jobs data, as market sentiment remained supported by strong ETF inflows and optimism around the Senate's upcoming vote on the CLARITY Act. The cryptocurrency reached its highest level since January, surging past $81,000 on May 5, 2026, before pulling back slightly to trade around $81,400. April spot BTC ETF inflows hit $2.44 billion, the strongest monthly figure since October 2025, indicating institutional accumulation during Q1's dip. The inflows have tightened available supply, potentially supporting further price increases. Bitcoin's breach of $81,000 marks a market recovery from Q1's downturn, with the cryptocurrency currently having the cleanest setup among major digital assets. The upcoming vote on the CLARITY Act and ETF inflows continue to support market sentiment.

stories.headline: Changing Geopolitics Are in Focus as France's Macron Kicks off Kenya Visit for an Africa Summit
stories.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron has begun a visit to Kenya, ahead of the Africa Forward Summit. The summit aims to showcase France's new policy for the continent, shifting from a dominant colonial power to a partnership of equals. This is the first time the summit is being held in an Anglophone country. Macron's visit comes as changing geopolitics are in focus. He met with Kenya's President William Ruto at State House in Nairobi, where they held a joint press conference. The Africa Forward Summit is expected to draw attention to France's revised approach to its relationships with African nations, marking a significant change in its historical role as a colonial power. Macron's visit and the summit are seen as key events in France's efforts to reposition itself on the continent.

stories.headline: Changing geopolitics in focus as France's Macron kicks off Kenya visit for Africa summit
stories.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron has begun a visit to Kenya ahead of the Africa Forward Summit, a gathering to showcase France's new policy for the continent. The summit, held for the first time in an Anglophone country, aims to demonstrate a shift from France's historical dominance as a colonial power to a partnership of equals. Kenya will host the event on May 11-12, with Presidents William Ruto and Macron in attendance. The Africa Forward Summit, previously known as the Africa-France Summit, marks a significant change in France's African diplomacy, expanding its engagement beyond Francophone nations. The event is expected to draw attention to the evolving geopolitics in the region and France's efforts to reposition itself as a partner to African countries. Macron's visit and the summit will focus on promoting cooperation and mutual understanding.

stories.headline: What To Know About AI’s Soaring Energy Appetite
stories.summary: AI's energy consumption is increasing due to rising investment, impacting local grids and overall tech energy demands. Energy companies, such as Virginia-based utility AES, cite AI power consumption as a leading contributor to new demand. By 2030, data centers could comprise up to 7.5% of total US electricity consumption, according to Boston Consulting Group. However, studies have found that certain AI applications, like generating text, are relatively energy-efficient. Creating 1,000 texts uses only about 16% of a full smartphone charge. As AI development continues, finding more efficient power solutions is crucial to mitigate its impact on the climate crisis. The growing energy demands of AI must be considered in the context of overall tech energy usage to ensure sustainable growth.

stories.headline: India’s ruling far-right BJP makes gains in state elections amid wave of anti-government working class protests
stories.summary: India's ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) has made significant gains in recent state assembly elections, winning control of West Bengal for the first time and retaining power in Assam and Puducherry. The party, led by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, is also poised to win in two of four key states, expanding its influence and weakening the opposition. The BJP's victories come amid a wave of anti-government protests from the working class. Defeated opponents have accused the BJP of cheating, but the party's strong performance is expected to solidify its position halfway into Modi's third term. The election results mark a major milestone for the BJP, which has been gaining ground in Indian politics in recent years. The party's wins are seen as a significant blow to the opposition.

stories.headline: US President Joe Biden faces backlash over proposed social security cuts in budget plan
stories.summary: US President Joe Biden's proposed budget plan includes social security reforms, sparking backlash. The plan aims to address the program's long-term viability, as the Social Security trust fund is predicted to be exhausted in eight years, resulting in a 23% automatic drop in payments. The proposed reforms include increases in benefits in several areas. However, the plan has drawn mixed reactions from Democrats and Republicans. Biden has defended his approach, criticizing previous administration's changes to the Social Security Administration. The reforms are part of a larger effort to ensure the program's sustainability, with Biden having recently signed a measure expanding Social Security benefits, amidst considerations of potential cuts by congressional Republicans and an advisory commission. The proposed changes reflect Biden's 2020 presidential campaign promises on Social Security reform.

stories.headline: European Union leaders meet to discuss ongoing migrant crisis and border control policies
stories.summary: European Union leaders are meeting to discuss the ongoing migrant crisis and border control policies. The EU is finalizing a major overhaul of its migration system, which includes streamlined deportations and increased detentions. Mainstream political parties have adopted tougher migration policies to counter far-right politicians. The migrant crisis is a significant humanitarian and political challenge, with millions fleeing conflict and persecution. The EU has been working to address the issue since 2015, with key developments in migration policy. A proposed deal with Paris aims to stop migrants crossing the Channel on small boats. The crisis involves several countries, including the UK, Germany, Greece, Italy, and France, with leaders seeking to find a solution to the ongoing issue. Migration statistics continue to be tracked, with the EU working to find a comprehensive solution.

stories.headline: Tensions rise between China and Taiwan as Chinese military conducts large-scale drills near Taiwanese waters
stories.summary: China's military conducted large-scale drills near Taiwanese waters, mobilizing army, naval, air force, and artillery units as part of its "Justice Mission 2025" exercises. The drills, which simulated the seizure of Taiwan, came after the US announced plans for arms sales to the island. Taiwan responded by deploying troops to rehearse repelling a potential invasion and coordinating with its coast guard to minimize the drills' impact. The Chinese military published a video showing warships being deployed, while Taiwan's coast guard deployed large ships to face off against Chinese vessels near its waters. The exercises ended months of relative calm across the Taiwan Strait, with China aiming to send a "serious warning" against any push for Taiwanese independence. The drills lasted for two days, heightening tensions between China and Taiwan.

stories.headline: India’s Stock Market Wipes Out ₹9 Trillion as investors panicked over rising crude oil prices and renewed pressure on the Indian
stories.summary: India's stock market lost ₹9 trillion as investors panicked over rising crude oil prices and pressure on the Indian Rupee. The equity market plunged amid a crude oil surge of up to 29% overnight, triggered by escalating West Asia tensions. The Sensex and Nifty plummeted around 2% due to the Middle East conflict involving the US and Iran. Heavy foreign institutional investor selling and global headwinds also contributed to the significant erosion of investor wealth. On a single day, around ₹12.78 trillion was lost in market capitalisation, with portfolios of prominent investors affected. The conflict in Iran has triggered a steep sell-off in Indian equities, resulting in substantial losses for investors. The market value loss exceeded ₹9 lakh crore, marking a significant downturn in India's equity markets.

stories.headline: Stock market crashes today: Sensex falls 1,000 points, Nifty50 trades below 23,900 oil prices jump amid Middle East tensions
stories.summary: The Indian stock market crashed today, with the Sensex falling over 1,000 points to 76,330 and the Nifty50 trading below 23,900. The decline is attributed to heavy selling in realty and consumer stocks, as well as rising oil prices amid Middle East tensions. The Sensex tumbled 1,313 points, or 1.70%, to 76,015.28, while the Nifty 50 plunged 1.50% to 23,815.85. The rupee also hit a record low due to US-Iran tensions. The market decline is a result of a fragile market sentiment, with the Sensex down 1,000 points or 1.29 percent at 76,664, and the Nifty falling 275 points or 1.14 percent to 23,898. The Indian equity benchmark indices, BSE Sensex and Nifty50, have been experiencing significant volatility in recent trade.

stories.headline: Bears howling: Sensex dives 1,150pts intraday, Nifty at 23,850; key reasons Stock market crash: Today's decline erased over ₹6 trillion from the Street
stories.summary: The Indian stock market experienced a significant decline, with the Sensex diving 1,150 points intraday and the Nifty reaching 23,850. The market capitalisation of BSE-listed companies decreased by over ₹6 trillion, standing at ₹4.67 trillion. The Sensex crashed 900 points, while the Nifty fell 250 points to 23,918.75. This decline is attributed to various factors, including weak Q3 earnings, FII outflows, and global uncertainties. The valuations of midcaps and smallcaps remain high, making them vulnerable to corrections. The Nifty 50 index has broken below the 22,200 support level, and the market is expected to be volatile. The BSE Sensex finished at 73,192, around 1,420 points lower than Thursday's close, amid a bloodbath on Dalal Street. The decline has erased a substantial amount of wealth from the market.

stories.headline: Sensex crashes almost 1,000 points; investors lose ₹4 lakh crore: Key factors behind stock market crash explained
stories.summary: The Sensex crashed almost 1,000 points, or over 1%, to an intraday low of 76,364, while the Nifty 50 plunged more than 1% to 23,896. The sharp sell-off resulted in a loss of nearly ₹4 lakh crore in investor wealth. The decline was attributed to various factors, including a 4% surge in crude oil prices due to US-Iran tensions. The total market capitalisation of NSE-listed companies decreased, wiping out considerable investor wealth. The stock market crash saw significant drops in key sectors, leading to a substantial erosion of market capitalization. The Sensex and Nifty experienced substantial losses, with the Sensex ending at lower levels and the Nifty below 23,900. The market downturn was driven by a combination of domestic and global factors, including geopolitical tensions and rising crude oil prices.

stories.headline: Almirall Continues Its Positive Trajectory in Q1 2026 in Line With Expectations - Led by 19.3% YoY Growth of Its European Dermatology Business
stories.summary: Almirall, a global pharmaceutical company, announced its Q1 2026 financial results, delivering on its growth trajectory in line with expectations. The company's European Dermatology business led the growth, with a 19.3% year-over-year (YoY) increase to €166.3 million. Net sales reached €291.0 million, a 2.2% YoY increase, with a 9% YoY growth over the last 12 months. The solid performance was driven by the European dermatology segment, which included a 13% YoY sales increase of Ilumetri, a treatment for plaque psoriasis, to €55 million. The company reiterated its 2026 guidance, indicating a continued positive trajectory in line with its long-term strategy. The growth reflects ongoing uptake in Germany and other recent European launches, with Almirall targeting peak sales of over €450 million by 2030 for certain products.

stories.headline: COCOBOD moves to reduce offshore borrowing with new cocoa funding framework
stories.summary: Ghana Cocoa Board (COCOBOD) is introducing a new financing framework for the cocoa sector, starting with the 2026/2027 crop season. The move aims to improve price stability and secure sustainable earnings for cocoa farmers. After 32 years of relying on offshore borrowing, COCOBOD will transition to self-financing to reduce dependency on external funds. The new framework includes a pricing mechanism with periodic reviews, potentially quarterly, to better shield farmers' incomes from global price volatility. This change marks a significant shift from the traditional cocoa syndication program, which has been in place for over three decades. The new funding model is expected to improve the overall stability of the cocoa sector and provide more predictable earnings for farmers. COCOBOD's decision is part of efforts to reduce offshore borrowing and promote self-sufficiency in the sector.

stories.headline: Cape Verde to Receive $10.5 Million From IMF After Reform Review
stories.summary: Cape Verde is set to receive $10.51 million from the International Monetary Fund (IMF) after a review of its reform programs. The country, which has limited natural resources and relies heavily on food imports, is implementing various reforms to strengthen its economy. IMF Mission Chief Martin Schindler announced the funding, which is part of the country's ongoing reform programs. Cape Verde's agricultural production is limited to only five of its ten main islands, with over 90% of its food being imported. The IMF funding aims to support the country's economic development and reform efforts. The total funding under the reform programs is $13.98 million, according to Schindler. The financial support is expected to help Cape Verde address its economic challenges and promote sustainable growth.

stories.headline: Kiwi May Defy Hedge-Fund Bears on Hawkish RBNZ, Analysts Say
stories.summary: The New Zealand dollar may rally despite bearish hedge-fund positioning, driven by a hawkish Reserve Bank of New Zealand (RBNZ) and potential de-escalation in the Middle East. The RBNZ is expected to raise interest rates by 25 basis points to combat elevated domestic inflation. The central bank's interest rate decision is announced after its scheduled policy meetings, with a hawkish stance leading to an increase in the Official Cash Rate (OCR) to curb inflation. Recently, the NZD/USD exchange rate surged to 0.6206 from 0.5771, indicating a potential rally. Analysts predict the Kiwi may defy bearish expectations and rise in the near-term, driven by the RBNZ's monetary policy and global geopolitical developments. The RBNZ's next move is closely watched, with a rate hike expected to support the New Zealand dollar.

stories.headline: OpenAI staff cashed out 6.6 billion dollars in one day, says report
stories.summary: OpenAI employees sold a combined $6.6 billion worth of stock in a single day in October 2025, with over 600 staff averaging $11 million each. The company had initially set a sale cap of $10 million per worker, but later raised it to $30 million due to strong investor demand. This secondary deal allowed employees to cash out, with some receiving up to $30 million. The sale comes after OpenAI announced a multi-billion dollar deal with AMD in October 2025, committing to purchase six gigawatts worth of AMD chips. The transaction is one of the largest single transfers of employee wealth in Silicon Valley, with staff turning paper gains into cash before the company's potential IPO. The average payout of $11 million per employee highlights the significant wealth created for OpenAI staff.

stories.headline: OpenAI lets employees cash out up to $30 million each in share sale, valuation hits $400 billion: Report
stories.summary: OpenAI allowed employees to cash out up to $30 million each in a share sale, valuing the company at approximately $400 billion. Around 75 participants, including current and former employees, sold the maximum amount allowed under the deal, totaling $6.6 billion. The share sale, which took place in October 2025, enabled over 600 employees to liquidate their equity. The $400 billion valuation is a significant milestone for the artificial intelligence company. The sale allowed employees to monetize their shares, with 75 individuals reaching the maximum limit of $30 million each. This secondary sale provided an opportunity for employees to realize significant financial gains from their equity holdings in the company.

stories.headline: The barista is human but an AI agent runs this experimental Swedish cafe
stories.summary: A new experimental cafe in Stockholm, Andon Café, is being run by an artificial intelligence agent nicknamed "Mona", developed by San Francisco-based startup Andon Labs. While human baristas still brew and serve coffee, Mona is in charge of managing the cafe. The AI agent handles tasks such as inventory management and customer service, but is struggling to turn a profit in Stockholm's competitive coffee market. Despite this, the cafe has made over $5,700 in sales. The experiment's duration is unclear, but it marks a unique attempt to integrate AI technology into the service industry. The cafe's performance will be closely watched to see if AI can successfully manage a commercial venture. Mona's role is a significant innovation in the use of AI in the hospitality sector.

stories.headline: OpenAI employees, both current and former, collectively sold $6.6 billion in shares during a secondary transaction in October 2025
stories.summary: OpenAI conducted a $6.6 billion secondary share sale in October 2025, valuing the company at approximately $400-500 billion. Over 600 current and former employees participated, selling their shares in a single coordinated transaction. On average, each person sold around $11 million worth of shares, with more than 75 participants cashing out the maximum permitted amount of $30 million each. This sale is one of the largest employee stock tender offers ever completed by a private technology company, cementing OpenAI's status as the most valuable private company in the world. The transaction allowed employees to liquidate their equity, with the company using it as a retention strategy to compete with rival offers from other tech companies.
